newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish insurer Compensa seeks listing by early '98.
newsitem.headline: Polish insurer Compensa seeks listing by early '98.

text.p: Polish insurer Compensa SA plans to issue up to 280,000 shares this year and to enter the main market of the Warsaw bourse late this year or early next, the firm's president said on Friday.

"The issue will probably be in two tranches...of altogether 70,000 to 280,000 shares," Krzysztof Lutostanski told Reuters, adding that a prospectus would be submitted to the securities commission by the end of this year's first half.

Lutostanski said one tranche would be open and the other offered to a specific investor or investors, likely from the financial sector, who would help the firm increase its current property insurance market share of 1.5 percent to four by the year 2000.
He said the company would size the open tranche so that after the issue is taken up by individual invesors at least 25 percent of all the firm's shares would be publicly traded.
Compensa, which employs 590, is 95-percent owned by Mostostal Export, which has 220,000 shares and 96.7 percent of shareholder votes.

Last year the firm, whose full name is Towarzystwo Ubezpieczeniowe Compensa SA, made a net profit of about 2.2 million zlotys on a gross premium of 81 million. In 1995 it netted 0.9 million zlotys on a gross premium of 40.5 million.
